{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 2013 | image = | dates = 5 May — 28 September 2013 | teams = 15 | connacht = | munster = Limerick | leinster = Dublin | ulster = Antrim | matches = 21 | poty = [[File: Colours of Clare.svg|border|20px]] [[Tony Kelly (hurler)|Tony Kelly]] | team = Clare | titles = 4th | captain = [[Patrick Donnellan]] | manager = [[Davy Fitzgerald]] | team2 = Cork | captain2 = [[Pa Cronin]] | manager2 = [[Jimmy Barry-Murphy]] | totalgoals = 48 (2.28 per game) | totalpoints = 710 (33.80 per game) | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Clare.svg|border|20px]] [[Colin Ryan (Clare hurler)|Colin Ryan]] (0–70) | previous = [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2012]] | next = [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2014]] }} The '''2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 126th staging of the All-Ireland championship since its establishment in 1887. The draw for the 2013 fixtures took place on 4 October 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/draws-made-for-leinster-and-munster-hurling-championship-569420.html|title=Draws made for Leinster and Munster hurling championship|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|date=4 October 2012|access-date=4 October 2012}} The championship began on 5 May 2013 and ended on 28 September 2013 with [[Clare GAA|Clare]] winning their fourth All Ireland title after a 5–16 to 3–16 win against [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the replayed [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=http://edit.setanta.com/ie/Articles/2013/09/28/Clare-claim-All-Ireland-SHC-crown/gnid-162270/|title=Clare claim All-Ireland SHC crown|date=28 September 2013|work=Setanta Sports|access-date=1 October 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131001153216/http://edit.setanta.com/ie/Articles/2013/09/28/Clare-claim-All-Ireland-SHC-crown/gnid-162270/|archive-date=1 October 2013}} [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were the [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|defending champions]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0930/339723-kilkenny-galway/|title=Imperious Kilkenny win All-Ireland at ease|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=30 September 2012|access-date=30 September 2012}} However, they were knocked out of the Leinster Championship by eventual Leinster champions [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] at the semi-final stage and [[Cork GAA|Cork]] saw them off in the All-Ireland quarter-final. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] won the [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster Championship]] for the first time since 1996. Cork defeated Dublin and [[Clare GAA|Clare]] defeated Limerick in the All-Ireland semi-finals. The 2013 Championship has been described by many as one of the best ever.{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/1002/477813-2013-hurling-championship-review/|title= What a hurling year we had in 2013|date=2 October 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=4 October 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/john-mullane-shocks-saves-and-some-magic-hurling-in-a-summer-to-savour-29639439.html|title= Shocks, saves and some magic hurling in a summer to savour |date=7 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=8 October 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/davy-rises-to-become-leader-of-the-pack-29857337.html|title= Davy rises to become leader of the pack|date=21 December 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 January 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hurlings-old-order-face-new-challenge-29873987.html|title= Hurling's old order face new challenge|date=30 December 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 January 2014}} In February 2014, the GAA announced that both the 2013 football and hurling Championships brought in €11.9m in gate receipts, an increase of €1.3m for the hurling championship.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-news/classic-hurling-year-reaps-dividend-3110346|title=Classic hurling year reaps dividend for the GAA|date=4 February 2014|work=Daily Mirror|access-date=5 February 2014}} The introduction of [[Hawk-Eye]] for Championship matches at Croke Park fell foul in a high-profile blunder by the computer system which led to use of Hawk-Eye being suspended during the All-Ireland semi-finals on 18 August. During the [[2013 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor game]] between Limerick and Galway, Hawk-Eye ruled a point for Limerick as a miss although the graphic showed the ball passing inside the posts, causing confusion around the stadium – the referee ultimately waved the valid point wide provoking anger from fans, viewers and TV analysts covering the game live.{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/gaas-hawkeye-stood-down-following-error-during-allireland-minor-semifinal-29508303.html|title=GAA's 'Hawkeye' stood down following error during All-Ireland minor semi-final|work=Irish Independent|date=18 August 2013|access-date=18 August 2013}} The system was subsequently stood down for the senior game which followed, owing to "an inconsistency in the generation of a graphic".{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/gaelic-games/23766418|title=Limerick to appeal after Hawk-Eye blunder in minor hurling game|work=BBC Sport|date=20 August 2013|access-date=20 August 2013}} Hawk-Eye admitted they were to blame and as a result Limerick, who were narrowly defeated after extra-time, announced they would be appealing over Hawk-Eye's costly failure.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0819/469099-hawk-eye-admits-to-human-error-at-croke-park/|title=Hawk-Eye admits to human error at Croke Park as Limerick confirm appeal|work=RTÉ Sport|date=19 August 2013|access-date=19 August 2013}} The incident drew attention from the UK, where Hawk-Eye had made its debut in English soccer's [[Premier League]] the day before.{{cite news|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/oukoe-uk-ireland-hawkeye-idUKBRE97I0YE20130819|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160107033045/http://uk.reuters.com/article/oukoe-uk-ireland-hawkeye-idUKBRE97I0YE20130819|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 [[Christy Ring Cup]] * [[London county hurling team|London]] === From Championship === Relegated to the [[Christy Ring Cup]] * None ==Teams== All teams from the [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2012 championship]] continued to line out in hurling's top tier in 2013. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were installed as the favourites to retain the All-Ireland title for a third consecutive year and to secure a remarkable tenth championship in fourteen seasons. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]], the last two teams to beat Kilkenny in championship hurling, were regarded as the two teams most likely to provide the strongest challenge to Kilkenny's supremacy once again. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] were ranked at 20/1 as they hoped to end a forty-year wait for the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]]. [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]], a team who won four [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster titles]] between 2002 and 2010, were seen as a team to have missed out on their chance at an All-Ireland title and were ranked at 25/1.{{cite news|url=http://www.paddypower.com/bet/gaa-hurling/all-ireland-shc|title=All-Ireland SHC Betting Odds|work=Paddy Power website|access-date=3 October 2012|archive-date=9 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130709192956/http://www.paddypower.com/bet/gaa-hurling/all-ireland-shc|url-status=dead}} [[London GAA|London]], the winners of the [[2012 Christy Ring Cup]], availed of their automatic right to promotion to the top tier and joined the Leinster championship.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20197211.html|title=Exiles pondering move to Leinster|work=[[Irish Examiner]]|access-date=30 September 2012|date=13 June 2012|first=Paul|last=Dollery}} Prior to the championship draw it emerged that Croke Park officials had written to the [[Laois GAA|Laois County Board]] inviting the county hurlers to participate in the [[2013 Christy Ring Cup]]. This was prompted by Laois's poor results during the previous few seasons.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/football/2012/0926/339156-laois-asked-to-play-in-christy-ring-cup/|title=Laois hurlers asked to play in Christy Ring Cup in 2013|work=[[RTÉ Sport]]|access-date=30 September 2012|date=26 September 2012}} In spite of these concerns Laois decided to remain in hurling's top tier and subsequently won two Leinster Championship matches.{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Laois/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=178176|title=Laois to remain in MacCarthy Cup|work=Hogan Stand Sunday Game]] Live'' and ''[[Championship Live]]'' respectively, with RTÉ showing the All-Ireland Final live. [[Setanta Sports]] and [[TG4]] showed highlights of matches in Ireland also. [[Setanta Sports Australia|Setanta Sports]] broadcasts live Championship matches in Australia. Also [[Setanta Sports Asia|Setanta Sports]] provided live matches in Asia. The ''Championship Live'' live programme was presented by [[Matt Cooper (Irish journalist)|Matt Cooper]], usually from an on-pitch studio with analysis from [[Daithí Regan]], [[Jamesie O'Connor]], and [[Nicky English]]. ''The Sunday Game'' live programme was presented by [[Michael Lyster]] with analysis usually from [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Ger Loughnane]], [[Liam Sheedy]], and [[Tomás Mulcahy]]. Highlights of all games were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired usually at 9:30pm on Sundays on [[RTÉ Two]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with analysis from [[Eddie Brennan]] and [[Donal Óg Cusack]]. Television coverage, in particular that of the Leinster Hurling Championship has been criticised in some circles. Neither RTÉ or TV3 decided to broadcast both Leinster Hurling Championship semi-finals. Both channels also declined the offer from the [[Leinster GAA]] to reschedule the Dublin – Kilkenny semi-final replay in order for it to be broadcast.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/leinster-council-coffers-to-be-swelled-by-tv-snubbing-of-hurling-replay-1.1442663|title=Leinster Council coffers to be swelled by TV snubbing of hurling replay|publisher=[[Irish Times]]|date=26 June 2013|access-date=1 July 2013}} These matches were broadcast live on television in Ireland {| class="wikitable" |- ! the first round of the Leinster championship, [[Craig Doyle (hurler)|Craig Doyle]] became the first player in the history of the championship to score [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship hat-tricks|three goals]] after coming on as a substitute. * In the Leinster semi-final replay, Dublin record a championship defeat of Kilkenny for the first time since [[1942 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1942]]. * The Leinster final was notable for a number of reasons. It was the first final to feature neither Kilkenny or Wexford since [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1990]]. The meeting of Dublin and Galway in the provincial decider was a first, while it was also their first championship meeting since 1942. Dublin maintained their 100% success rate over Galway, with a sixth win from six meetings, to claim the Leinster title for the first time since [[1961 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1961]]. * The Munster final between Cork and Limerick was the sides' first meeting at this stage of the championship since [[1992 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1992]]. Limerick's victory was their first provincial title since [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1996]]. * Cork and Kilkenny's All-Ireland quarter-final meeting at [[Semple Stadium]] was their first championship meeting outside of [[Croke Park]] since [[1907 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1907]]. * For the first time since [[1951 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1951]], Kilkenny did not play a single championship game in Croke Park. It is also the first time since [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1996]] that Kilkenny failed to qualify for an All-Ireland semi-final. * The All-Ireland semi-final between Cork and Dublin was the sides' first meeting in the All-Ireland series since [[1952 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1952]]. * The All-Ireland semi-final between Clare and Limerick was the sides' first ever meeting at this stage of the championship. * The All-Ireland final was notable for a number of reasons. It was the second ever all-Munster All-Ireland decider and the first time since [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1997]] that this has happened. It was the first time since [[2004 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2004]] that neither the Leinster or Munster champions contested the All-Ireland final. It was the first ever All-Ireland final meeting of Cork and Clare. For the second successive year the All-Ireland final ended in a draw. The replay was also unique as it was the first All-Ireland final to be played on a Saturday. * Clare win their fourth All-Ireland title to draw level with Galway and Offaly as joint seventh on the all-time roll of honour. * Clare's victory also marked the first time a team outside the traditional "[[Big Three (hurling)|Big Three]]" of hurling (Kilkenny, Cork and Tipperary) had won the All-Ireland since [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in [[1998 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1998]]. ===Notable matches=== 2013 will be remembered as a year that the traditionally weaker counties made an impact. Limerick who hadn't been in an All-Ireland Final since 2007 beat reigning Munster Champions Tipperary by 3 points, 1–18 to 1–15 in a Munster semi-final. Clare under David Fitzgerald held off Waterford in a Munster Quarter-final winning by 2–20 to 1–15. They were overcome by a stronger Cork side in the Munster Semi-final losing 0–23 to 0–15. Laois made it to the Leinster semi-final where they put it up to Galway even leading by a point at half time [0-08 – 0-07], but Galway's physicality helped them run out 7 point victors [2–17 – 1–13]. Dublin came into the season after a disappointing 2012 season and a hammering by Tipperary in the league semi-final [4–20 0–17]. In their Leinster Quarter-final they drew with Wexford, 1–17 – 1–17 but in the replay ran out easy 8 point winners, 1–17 – 0–12. Offaly jumped to a 1–01 to 0–00 start against Kilkenny in their quarter-final clash. They led at half time by 2–06 to 0–11 but failed to stop Kilkenny, although they managed to score 4 goals as Kilkenny won 0–26 to 4–09. In their semi-final Dublin ran at Kilkenny and held out for a draw in the match, 0–17 – 1–14. In the replay Dublin raced to a 0–04 to 0–01 lead after 10 mins and lead 0–11 to 0–07 at half time. They ran out 3 point winners, 1–17 0–17. Dublin made it to a Leinster final while Kilkenny where exiled to the qualifiers for a second year. Kilkenny fought hard against Tipperary and sent them out of the Championship, winning by three points. Dublin beat Galway by 12 points to claim their first Leinster title in 52 years.{{cite web |url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0707/461064-dublin-galway/ |title=Dublin 2–25 Galway 2–13 |date=7 July 2013 |access-date=15 September 2013 |publisher=RTÉ Sport}} Kilkenny knocked out Waterford in the final stage of the Qualifiers after extra time. Carlow lead Wexford for most of their game in the qualifiers, until a late goal sent them out. At the quarter-final stage, Cork knocked out Championship favourites and title holders, Kilkenny. Clare knocked out Galway, the previous year's runners-up. Both Provincial Champions were beaten in the semi-finals. Cork defeated Dublin after the game of the season by 1–24 to 1–19, and Clare beat Limerick by 1–22 to 0–18.
